key_insight: A Fourier neural operator surrogate learns to correct inexpensive Boussinesq natural-convection simulations toward compressible-flow accuracy with a single model evaluation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical CFD acceleration strategy for thermal-flow design studies where near-compressible fidelity is desired without paying the full cost of high-fidelity simulation.
method: Generate matched low-fidelity Boussinesq and high-fidelity compressible simulation pairs.
Train a Fourier neural operator on 2D and 3D natural-convection cases.
Use parallel implicit monolithic mixed FEM solvers in FEniCSx, validated against COMSOL and literature benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across all flow variables and test distributions, the surrogate reports SSIM close to 1 and mean-squared-error reductions from one to nearly three orders of magnitude relative to Boussinesq predictions.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of paired training data, so extrapolation beyond the simulated flow regimes may be unreliable.
paper_title: A Neural Surrogate Approach for Simulating Natural Convection Problems
